first_impression.rationale: Same hero as v4 (evidence/index-phone-top.png): an uncomposed photograph of a hand and teal phone, the 'Open until 8 p.m. today' chip, the white 'Plans from' logo bar and the H1 'Pick up a phone. Ask a real person.' v5 fixes the header tagline, which now breaks evenly as 'Bell Authorised Retailer / on Bovaird Dr W' instead of orphaning 'Dr W', but it is still two lines above two rows of nav pills, the hero buttons still sit under the sticky Call / Directions / Book bar on the first screen, and 'Brampton' is still not visible above the fold.

imagery_quality.rationale: Twelve Pexels photos share one grade and read as a coherent set; the hero, repair-mat, cracked-screen and living-room shots are sharp (measured sharpness above 0.85, AVIF/WebP/JPEG, pages 97-217 KiB) and no page carries a composite (evidence/imagery-sheet.png, index-phone.png). Held back by: marks I could still read at full size (certification marks and Li-ion lettering on the battery label in repair-mat-16x10-1600.jpg, partial wristband lettering in concert-4x5-1000.jpg, faint retouch smudges where the Apple logo and the train ticket-machine sticker were), the same four phone photos (two-phones, concert, train, living-room) repeating on home, brands, mobile and deals, generic stock people (seniors, cafe, video call) and no real photo of the store. The social preview og-image.jpg is a composed card (hero plus wordmark, headline and logos), the very pattern Mark disliked.

logo_integration.rationale: All eight logo files match the contract hashes and in the screenshots they are undistorted, uncropped and uncoloured on white rounded plates: the 'Plans from' bar on the home hero (index-phone-top.png), bottom-left plates on the two-phones, concert, train and living-room photos (deals-phone.png, mobile-phone.png, brands-phone.png) and heading plates beside the Bell sections. Plates never sit on identifiable-person photos (the Bell plate on brands.html and mobile.html is in the text column beside the cafe photo). Held back by: the 'by Bell' tag in the Lucky Mobile logo is tiny at phone size, plates cover a photo corner (on deals-phone the first Bell plate is partly under the sticky bar) and the README still lists brand sign-off as open.

service_clarity.rationale: Home explains each of Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile in one line ('One network, three ways in'), then internet and TV starting from your address, repairs quoted first and number porting in three steps; brands.html adds a 'short version' table that stacks into three cards on phone, and the facts I checked match Bell and press sources. Held back by: the offer cards on index.html and deals.html show '$XX/mo' and 'Replace with this month's ... offer' instructions, the opening of brands-phone.png is a 4-line H1 and 6-line lead with no photo or logo, and SmartPay is re-explained on four pages.

navigation_wayfinding.rationale: The same six plain labels on every page (Deals, Compare plans, Phones, Internet & TV, Repairs, Find us) with the current page in a dark pill, a header Call button, the sticky Call / Directions / Book bar, a skip link, anchor pills on brands.html and a footer index (every *-phone-top.png). Held back by: the pills wrap onto two rows at 390 px (about 110 px of every first screen), Home is reachable only through the logo and the footer, and 'Compare plans' versus 'Phones' takes a moment to tell apart.

conversion_paths.rationale: The phone call is the main path and it is everywhere: header Call, the sticky bar, 'Call 647-707-1093' in hero and closing bands, tel: links on every offer card, 'Directions in Google Maps', plus a repair request form and a visit form with a tel input, autocomplete and a honeypot (visit-phone.png, repairs-phone.png). Held back by: the hero buttons sit under the sticky bar on the first phone screen, 'Book a visit' is a free-text day/time request rather than a slot, I did not submit the forms (the demo posts to thanks.html), and 'Ask about this offer' on placeholder cards leads to a call about an offer that does not exist yet.

distinctiveness.rationale: Against design 1 the look is clearly different: photo-led white page, one sans family, Bell-blue actions; measured visual similarity 0.11, palette distance 15.7, no shared headings, and page titles, H1s and leads are new. But my own sentence pairing found design-1 sentences lightly reworded rather than rewritten (privacy.html, repairs.html, mobile.html steps, deals.html small lines, Member Benefits and Fibe TV lines; listed in notes), the nav labels Deals, Internet & TV and Repairs are identical to design 1 (the allowed maximum of 3), and the page skeleton and section order match design 1.

brand_identity.rationale: The footer is now a slightly darker tint with a 4 px red top rule (visible on the index-desktop.png and brands-desktop.png footers), which picks up the red of the T Wireless wordmark and separates the footer from the mist bands above it. It is a small gain; the page is otherwise unchanged, so actions are still Bell blue on white, the wordmark is the only store colour and there is no store photography.

trust_signals.rationale: Checkable and visible: 'Bell Authorised Retailer' on every page, address, phone and hours repeated, an open/closed chip, a named contact (Ali), an accessible-entrance line, a privacy page, an honest 'stock photos, not our store, staff or customers' footer, 'Example offer' badges and price and terms disclaimers. Bell's own store locator confirms the name, phone, address and 10-8 daily hours, but lists postal code L6X 5K7 where the site shows L6X 0G3 (flagged in the README). Held back by: I could not open the Google listing to check '4.1 on Google, from 91 reviews', there is no real photo of the store or team, and wheelchair access, trade-in credit and the photo-ID requirement have no source and are not on the owner checklist.

information_economy.rationale: Sentences are short and mostly earn their place, and FAQ answers sit in accordions. But facts recur: SmartPay on home, brands, mobile and deals, Fibe TV on brands and internet-tv, the Virgin Plus internet/TV notice on brands and internet-tv, porting steps on home, mobile and FAQ, hours in about six places. The home page is about 7,240 CSS px tall on a phone (measured 7,239 in v5) with ten sections, and each deal card carries a title, price, detail and a grey 'Replace with ...' line (deals-phone.png).

typography_hierarchy.rationale: Unchanged scale (15, 17, 20, 25, 28, 42 px; hero ratio 2.47; one H1 per page). v5 removes the orphaned 'Dr W' in the header tagline with balanced wrapping (every *-phone-top.png) and adds clearer space under H2s. Still held back by the slashed zeros in numerals ('1Ø a.m.', '7Ø7'), the 4-line H1 on brands-phone-top.png and the 15 px grey instruction text in the offer cards.

grid_whitespace_rhythm.rationale: v5 fixes the specific faults I flagged in v4: 'The short version' now has air between the heading and the first card (brands-phone.png), the checklist and the 'Google reviewers rate us' line are separated (visit-phone.png), and the forms' H2s have more room above their intro text (repairs-phone.png, visit-phone.png). The rhythm is now even on phone. Still held back by: deals-desktop.png 'Ask about this offer' buttons at different heights with an empty slot in row two, the index-desktop.png FAQ leaving the right half empty and a blank band under the store card on visit-desktop.png.

mobile_ergonomics.rationale: Sticky three-target action bar with safe-area padding, 44-50 px pills, chips and buttons, a tel input type with autocomplete on the forms, FAQ accordions, a map that loads only on tap, zero horizontal overflow, minimum 15 px text, Lighthouse 99-100 with LCP at most 2.04 s and CLS near 0. Held back by: the sticky bar covers in-flow CTAs on first screens (hero buttons on index-phone-top.png, the Directions button on visit-phone-top.png), the two-row nav repeats on every page, Call appears twice at once (header and bar) and the home page is about 7,240 px long.

notes:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW, design 2 'In hand', v5-candidate (v4 plus CSS-only polish). I confirmed what changed: the 11 built HTML pages are identical to v4 apart from the stylesheet cache-buster, all 268 other site files (photos, fonts, logos, scripts) are byte-identical, and site.css differs in four rules only: a darker footer tint (--foot #e8edf3) with a 4 px red top rule, text-wrap: balance on the header tagline, 12-18 px more space after headings and checklists (.ticks + p, .form-split h2 + p, .visit h2 + .ticks, h2 + .table-wrap). I compared the v4 and v5 screenshots region by region (header on every *-phone-top.png, brands-phone.png 'The short version', visit-phone.png checklist and rating line, repairs-phone.png form heading, footers on index-phone.png and index-desktop.png) and looked at v5's phone tops and brands and visit desktop pages. measured.json for v5: 305 checks, 0 failed, same Lighthouse and distinctness numbers.

Scores: v4 scores carried over where nothing visible changed. Changed because of what I see in v5: grid_whitespace_rhythm 3.5 to 4.0 (the spacing faults are gone), first_impression, typography_hierarchy and brand_identity re-scored with the new header and footer (no change in score, rationale updated), and page roles visit hierarchy 4.0 to 4.5 (checklist and rating line now separate, heading spacing fixed). brands.html hierarchy stays 3.5: its spacing is fixed but the opening is still a 4-line H1 and 6-line lead with no photo or logo. Photos and copy are unchanged, so every accuracy gate is carried over from v4 with the same reasons.

ACCURACY GATES SET TO FALSE (4 of 8)
1. no_third_party_brand_marks_in_photos = false. I found no consumer-brand name or logo (no Apple, Samsung, carrier or retailer wordmark) legible anywhere, and tesseract (1x-3x, CLAHE and inverted variants) over the served JPEGs found no brand words. But marks remain that read at full size, and an earlier run of this check was wrong in just this way, so I am not passing it: (a) site/assets/img/photos/repair-mat-16x10-1600.jpg, battery label at about x285-385, y310-370: a UL-style certification mark, a Li-ion recycling symbol and 'Li-ion' lettering, with a faint smear where the Apple logo was erased; the same label is in the unused repair-mat-4x5-1000.jpg; tiny white lettering on a small part near x1120-1320, y650-780 and dark printed blocks on the shield near x1320-1370, y490-515 are not readable; (b) concert-4x5-1000.jpg, wristband at lower right, about x840-945, y1130-1200: partial event lettering '...Y GA' (also at the lower right of concert-16x9-960.jpg); not retouched; (c) not logos but product-identifying: unboxing-16x10-1280.jpg shows an iPhone XS retail carton (top right, about x770-1055, y0-240) and MacBook-style key legends 'tab, caps lock, shift, fn, control, opt' (top right corner, x1130-1280, y0-260); the concert phone screen shows the iOS camera interface. Severity is low: nothing here names a brand a visitor would recognise at display size, and the fix is one more retouch pass or a crop. Checked and clean at full size: hand-blue-phone (the hero), two-phones, train (operator logo and ticket-machine sticker gone, red device plain; only a faint smudge remains at about x270-310, y1170-1210 of train-4x5-1000.jpg), cafe-business (seven polo-emblem regions erased, no copies found), family-tv, living-room (TV bezel, media boxes and wall art show no marks), video-call, seniors-phone, cracked-screen.
2. copy_written_for_this_design = false. The measured checks pass (phrase overlap 0.065, reused sentences 0, shared headings 0, shared nav labels at the limit of 3) and titles, descriptions, H1s, leads and section headings are all new. But the 4-gram test cannot see synonym swaps, and pairing sentences by hand against design 1's built pages shows design-1 sentences lightly reworded: privacy.html 'When you send a visit or repair request, we get your name, your phone number and whatever you write in the form.' (design 1: 'When you send a repair or visit request, we receive your name, phone number and the details you type into the form.'); privacy.html 'To ask about your details or have them deleted, ring 647-707-1093, email twireless965@gmail.com, or come into the store at 965 Bovaird Dr W, Unit 1, Brampton.' (design 1: 'To ask about your information or have it deleted, call us at ..., email ..., or visit the store at ...'); repairs.html 'Rather talk it through? Call 647-707-1093 or email twireless965@gmail.com.' (design 1: 'Prefer to talk? Call 647-707-1093 or email twireless965@gmail.com.', identical second sentence); mobile.html steps 'Pick your plan and phone / We talk through Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile with you.' and 'We move the number' (design 1: 'Choose your plan and phone / We go through the options from Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile with you.' and 'We move your number'); repairs.html step 'Book, or just come in / Request a time below, or walk in every day from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.' (design 1: 'Book or walk in / Book below, or come by every day from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.'); deals.html 'Tell us what you use your phone for and what you pay today.' and 'Nothing in this group right now. Ring us and we'll tell you what's coming.' (design 1: 'Tell us how you use your phone and what you pay now.' and 'No deals in this group right now. Call us and we'll tell you what's on.'); brands.html 'Perks on food, shopping, travel and entertainment, found in the My Benefits app.' and 'We can make the move with you, or line it up against Lucky Mobile prepaid.' (design 1: 'Offers on entertainment, travel, shopping and food in the My Benefits app.' and '... make the switch with you, or compare it with Lucky Mobile prepaid.'); internet-tv.html 'Live TV and on-demand shows in the Fibe TV app.' (design 1: 'Live and on-demand TV in the Fibe TV app.'). Also mobile.html 'We sell iPhone and Android phones' (design 1: 'We carry ...'). Fix: rewrite roughly ten lines. The home hero, lead, headings and most body copy are genuinely new, so this is a small residue, not the 'exactly the same copy' Mark complained about.
3. unverified_flagged_for_owner = false. The README 'Before launch' list is thorough (postal code, Sunday hours, example offers, base URL, Bell family page items, repair list and quotes, walk-ins and callbacks, Ali named, carrier logo sign-off, privacy page, Google rating refresh, stock photos) and the site itself flags example offers and stock photos. But these claims are stated as fact on the site and are neither sourced nor on the checklist: 'Wheelchair-accessible entrance' (home trust strip, FAQ, visit.html; it comes only from accessible_entrance: true in src/site.json); 'South side of Bovaird, just east of Chinguacousy Rd' and the drawn map sketch (README says about 150 m east of the intersection; no instruction to confirm); 'Trade in. Got an old phone? Ask if it can earn credit toward the new one.' (brands.html, mobile.html); 'Bring government-issued photo ID' (mobile.html step 1, the home page steps and FAQ, visit.html, internet-tv.html); Bell's own number-transfer page asks for an account number, IMEI or PIN, not ID; 'the offers keep changing' (Member Benefits, brands.html). The README also says the hero is 'unedited' while the table row says the maker's name was retouched out.
4. no_fabricated_offers_or_reviews = false, only because I could not verify, not because I found anything invented. I saw no invented offer: every deal card is badged 'Example offer' with '$XX/mo' placeholders, and the site quotes no customer review. The line '4.1 on Google, from 91 reviews' (home trust strip, visit.html) comes from the store's Google listing, which I cannot open and could not find through search; I will not guess. The owner or the main session needs to confirm it against the listing (and it carries no 'as of' date, so it will go stale).

ACCURACY GATES SET TO TRUE (4 of 8)
- content_matches_sources = true. Checked in this session: Bell SmartPay, 24 monthly payments at 0% APR, $0 down, eligible 2-year plan, Bell credit approval (support.bell.ca 'what is bell smartpay'; bell.ca/business SmartPay page says 'on approved credit'). Device Return Option: choice at the end of the 2-year term, deferred amount credited if the phone is returned in good working condition, charged if kept (support.bell.ca Device_Return_Option). Virgin Plus prepaid ends January 15, 2027 and customers must move to a monthly plan to keep their number (MobileSyrup, 18 Aug 2026). Virgin Plus stopped taking new home internet and TV customers in Ontario on January 14, 2026 and current customers keep plan, pricing and equipment (iPhone in Canada, 14 Jan 2026). Member Benefits: built in, no extra cost, no points, My Benefits app, entertainment/travel/retail/food (WhistleOut guide). Lucky Mobile: Bell's prepaid brand (MobileSyrup 2017), 'no long-term commitments, credit checks or data overages' (bell.ca prepaid page), runs on Bell's network (WhistleOut), slower speeds after the full-speed allotment (MobileSyrup). Fibe TV: Bell Streamer, Apple TV, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV and Chromecast are supported, Bell Internet is required, Crave is included in some bundles, downloads exist (support.bell.ca Fibe TV app; bell.ca Fibe TV app). Porting: do not cancel the old service first and the new provider cancels it (support.bell.ca number-transfer page; CRTC 'do not cancel your service before you switch'). Bell's store locator lists T Wireless at 965 Bovaird Drive West with phone 647 707-1093 and 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. Small nuances only: recordings can be downloaded only with a PVR and on-demand downloads are capped at 10 titles (the site's 'recorded or picked on demand can be downloaded' is a simplification), and the business SmartPay line omits 'on approved credit'. I could not open virginplus.ca or luckymobile.ca (not on this session's fetch allowlist), so the Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile claims rest on bell.ca and the press sources above.
- photos_licensed_for_commercial_use = true. I opened all 12 Pexels photo pages (11772521, 7190924, 5398928, 17964711, 7251087, 14798018, 19899066, 4049991, 31862950, 11921157, 10375885, 6975187): each shows 'Free' and the photographer named on credits.html. The Pexels License allows commercial use and edits without attribution and forbids implied endorsement, identifiable people in a bad light, selling unaltered copies, redistribution and use in a trademark or business name; none of that is breached. Pexels pages mention no model release for the four identifiable-person photos (family-tv, video-call, cafe-business, seniors-phone), which the licence does not promise either.
- no_photo_implies_store_staff_or_customers = true. Every page footer and credits.html say the photos are stock and none show the store, staff or customers; alt text is neutral ('A woman in a cafe checking her phone'); no testimonial, quote or 'our team' copy sits near any people photo; carrier plates are never placed on identifiable-person photos. A visitor could still read the cafe photo beside the Bell for business heading as a Bell customer, but the disclaimer covers it.
- carrier_logos_unaltered_on_clean_plates = true. The sha256 of bell.svg, virgin-plus.png, virgin-plus.webp, lucky-mobile.svg and the T Wireless logo files match logos.files in the contract; in every screenshot the logos are undistorted, uncropped, uncoloured and on white plates (checked on the home hero bar, deals, mobile, brands, internet-tv). The og-image.jpg card puts the logos straight on a white card rather than on plates; it is not a page image.

3. Placeholder offers show to customers: '$XX/mo' and 'Replace with this month's ... offer and its conditions.' / 'Replace with your repair offer, or remove this card.' on index.html (3 cards under 'On offer this month') and deals.html (5 cards).
